risks: Cortical parcellation-by-angle for 12 zones on a noisy continuous mesh is inherently fiddly hand-tuning (unlike the tech scout's simpler 5-6 lobe example) and may need several visual-iteration passes before boundaries look anatomically plausible and don't leave unassigned or overlapping vertices — build a temporary flat-color-by-regionId debug material early (step 9) specifically to make this tunable by eye rather than guessing blind.

UnrealBloomPass plus any MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission use are the two most expensive parts of the render stack on integrated/hybrid GPUs; without the auto-detect+toggle from step 5 actually gating them by default, laptop frame rate could drop well below 60fps once ~28 tagged objects, InstancedMesh particles, and bloom are all active simultaneously.

Glossary auto-linking via regex is a classic source of subtle bugs: substring collisions (e.g. 'ERP' matching inside 'N170'/'N400' explanations, or 'memory' matching inside 'working memory') and re-wrapping text that's already inside a just-inserted span if linkTerms is ever called twice on the same node — must use longest-match-first ordering, word-boundary regex, and a single linkTerms pass per fresh string only.

The Izhikevich v² term is numerically stiff; any deviation from the two-half-step-per-1ms discipline (e.g. a naive single 1ms Euler step, or checking the spike threshold only once per rendered frame instead of after every sub-step) can silently corrupt spike timing/counts or diverge to NaN, which would then propagate invisibly into the raster/rate canvases as blank or frozen plots rather than an obvious crash — the isFinite guard and per-substep threshold check from step 14 are not optional polish, they are load-bearing correctness requirements.

Content volume is large (28 region cards, 8 pathways × ~5 steps × 4 text fields each, 38 glossary entries, 6 neuromodulator write-ups, 13 misconception items) — transcribing all of it correctly into JS literals without truncation or copy-paste drift is itself a meaningful source of errors; a step should diff the embedded DATA objects' counts (28/8/38/6/13) against the research JSON before considering content-entry done.

Modeling the insula as an always-visible discrete primitive is an anatomical simplification (it is folded cortex, not a subcortical nucleus) — if left unexplained this repeats exactly the 'phrenology-style, one-bump-one-fixed-location' framing the content research explicitly warns against; the insula's card and/or a brief inline note must say it is normally hidden inside the lateral sulcus and is shown exposed here for clickability.

Copy-overclaiming risk is systemic, not confined to one slider: the Dopamine slider must never read as implementing reward-prediction-error/learning, the neuron population must never be narrated as 'thinking' or as literally being any named real circuit (amygdala/VTA/hippocampal wiring), and pathway ms values for motor-skill-learning and sleep-consolidation must stay visibly labeled schematic-order-only rather than literal timings — this needs a deliberate final read-through pass (step 17), not just careful first-drafting.

CDN version pinning must be exact and identical across the core module and every addon import; mixing versions (or ever switching to three@0.180.0+, where three.module.js internally imports a sibling three.core.js) changes nothing functionally through the CDN but is a reason to avoid 'upgrading' the pin later without re-verifying every addon URL still resolves against it.
open_questions_for_user: Should the two hemispheres of paired subcortical structures (amygdala, hippocampus, thalamus, caudate/putamen, globus pallidus, nucleus accumbens) be modeled as two independently clickable meshes sharing one info card (anatomically correct, doubles click targets to ~40) or as a single midline-representative primitive per structure (fewer targets, simpler lesion-mode UI, slightly less anatomically literal)? The plan above defaults to two meshes sharing one card — confirm this default is fine before step 4, since it affects the subcortical primitive count and the lesion-mode 'reset all' bookkeeping.

Should Atlas Explore's lesion mode have any cross-mode effect (e.g., lesioning both hippocampi shows a note or visibly disables the recall_word/sleep_consolidation pathways), or should the three modes stay fully independent for this build, with only a textual 'see also' cross-reference in the region cards? The plan defaults to fully independent modes to keep scope bounded — this only matters if he wants the app to feel more like one connected simulation rather than three separate tools.

Is a light-mode/theme toggle wanted at all, or should the app deliberately commit to the single dark glassy look described here with no light variant? Nothing in the brief requires light mode and the visual design above assumes dark-only; confirming this avoids doing (or skipping) unnecessary theming work.

problems.issue: Citation error in the fear_response pathway (step 1, thalamus): the content attributes the '~10-20ms thalamic/hypothalamic, ~20-30ms amygdala' MEG timing to 'Luo et al., 2007, PNAS'. Verified via search: this is Luo, Holroyd, Jones, Hendler & Blair (2007), 'Neural dynamics for facial threat processing as revealed by gamma band synchronization using MEG', published in NeuroImage 34(2):839-847, DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2006.09.023 — NOT PNAS. The numeric latencies themselves are reported correctly by the content, only the journal is wrong.
problems.fix: Change the citation to 'Luo et al., 2007, NeuroImage' throughout (data model and any UI text that names the source).

problems.issue: Internal numerical inconsistency in the fear_response pathway: step 1 cites MEG source-localized amygdala activity 'by ~20-30ms' (Luo et al. 2007, NeuroImage), then step 2 cites intracranial-recorded amygdala responses beginning '~74-88ms' (Méndez-Bértolo et al. 2016, Nature Neuroscience, confirmed via search: iERP onset ~74ms) for the SAME structure in the SAME pathway — a ~3x discrepancy that is never reconciled. This matters because MEG beamformer source-localization of a small, deep structure like the amygdala is itself a genuinely contested method (spatial resolution/leakage concerns), while the intracranial number is far better grounded; presenting both as if they simply describe sequential stages invites a careful user to notice the numbers contradict each other and lose trust in the pathway feature's precision.
problems.fix: Either drop the ultra-fast MEG-based amygdala figure and keep only the intracranial ~74-88ms number (recommended, since it's the stronger evidence), or explicitly flag in the step text that these are two competing estimates from different methods with different reliability, not two sequential events.

problems.issue: Missing myth-flag parallel to the amygdala one: the Broca's/Wernicke's area cards (and the recall_word / reading_sentence pathways built on them) present the classical 'Broca = production, Wernicke = comprehension, arcuate fasciculus disconnection' model as essentially settled. Verified via search: this classic model is widely considered obsolete in modern aphasiology (Tremblay & Dick, 2016, Brain and Language, titled 'Broca and Wernicke are dead'; also Dronkers et al. 2007's MRI re-analysis of Broca's actual preserved patient brain — 'Tan'/Leborgne — showing the lesion extended well beyond 'Broca's area' into the insula and subcortical white matter). Language comprehension/production are now understood as distributed across a wider network (arcuate/uncinate/inferior fronto-occipital/middle longitudinal fasciculi), not two clean boxes connected by one tract. The project's own accuracy_pitfalls list explicitly warns against 'one bump = one fixed faculty' framing and calls out the amygdala for this, but the identical issue is left unflagged for language — arguably the single most iconic case of this exact myth in the field.
problems.fix: Add an accuracy_pitfalls entry and a caveat note on the broca/wernicke region cards and the two pathways that use them: the classic double-dissociation model is a useful teaching simplification, but modern lesion/imaging/tractography work shows language relies on a more distributed network, and Broca's own 'Tan' case had damage well beyond the area later named for him.

problems.issue: Scope: three.js pathways/plan bundles three technically-independent, individually large subsystems into one 'first prototype' — a procedural 3D neuroanatomy atlas (28 regions, 12-zone hand-tuned cortical parcellation), 8 fully-narrated animated pathway scenarios (40 steps x 4 text fields each), and a numerically delicate 150-neuron Izhikevich spiking network with 6 neuromodulator mappings and 4 live plots. Each of these alone is a substantial build (the plan's own 17-step build sequence and stated risks section implicitly concede this). Combined into a single index.html with zero build step, the realistic risk is that content-entry errors (28 x 7 fields, 8 x 5 x 4 fields, 38 glossary entries, 6 neuromodulator write-ups = very large hand-transcribed literal count) and three separate sources of runtime bugs (raycasting/parcellation, animation timeline state machine, ODE integration stability) compound, making 'no console errors across all three modes' a high-effort bar to actually hit for a v1.
problems.fix: For a genuine first prototype, ship one mode fully polished before building all three — Atlas Explore is the lowest technical risk (no animation state machine, no ODE stability concerns) and would validate the procedural-brain rendering approach on its own. If all three must ship together, cut pathway count to 3-4 and region count to ~15-18 (one clean set covering each major system: vision, language, memory, emotion, movement) for v1, expanding afterward.

problems.issue: The hypothalamus card presents the classic ventromedial-hypothalamus-as-satiety-center / lateral-hypothalamus-as-feeding-center 'dual center' model via 'classic animal studies' without noting that this specific model is now considered outdated. Verified via search (PubMed 16412483, 'The rise, fall, and resurrection of the ventromedial hypothalamus...'): since the 1994 discovery of leptin and the arcuate nucleus's role, the field has moved from discrete 'centers' to a distributed, hormonally-integrated model (leptin/ghrelin, POMC/AgRP neurons projecting to multiple hypothalamic nuclei). This is the same category of oversimplification the project explicitly flags for the amygdala, just not applied here.
problems.fix: Add a one-line caveat to the hypothalamus card: the classic 'feeding center vs. satiety center' framing is a historical simplification; modern work centers on the arcuate nucleus integrating hormonal signals (leptin, ghrelin) across a distributed hypothalamic network.

problems.issue: M1's lesion_effects/functions describe it as 'major origin of the corticospinal tract' without qualification. This is defensible but can read as 'M1 = the motor output pathway,' when a substantial share of corticospinal fibers actually originate from premotor cortex, supplementary motor area, and parietal cortex (Dum & Strick's classic primate tracing work), not just M1 — another instance of the single-region-single-function framing the project otherwise tries to avoid.
problems.fix: Soften to 'a major source (alongside premotor and supplementary motor cortex) of the corticospinal tract' or add a one-line note.

problems.issue: Substantia nigra lesion_effects states 'symptoms typically appear only after roughly 50-80% of these neurons are already lost,' conflating two distinct, commonly-cited-but-different statistics: SNc dopaminergic cell-body loss (usually cited around 50-60% at symptom onset) versus striatal dopamine/terminal depletion (usually cited higher, ~70-80%). Presenting a single merged 50-80% range obscures that these are two different measurements with different typical values.
problems.fix: Either cite the cell-loss figure (~50-60%) and the terminal-depletion figure (~70-80%) separately, or soften to a vaguer 'the majority' framing rather than implying one precise range covers both metrics.

problems.issue: The vmPFC/OFC card cites Phineas Gage's personality change as established fact ('showed dramatic personality change') without any caveat. Verified via search (Macmillan's historical review, Science History Institute, Frontiers in Human Neuroscience 2022): the dramatic 'became a foul-mouthed, unreliable drifter' narrative rests on a single ~300-word secondhand account from Harlow that never quotes Gage directly, and later generations of textbooks progressively embellished the story to fit 19th-century phrenology-adjacent localization debates. Gage is arguably the single most over-mythologized case in cognitive neuroscience, and this project explicitly aims to flag exactly this kind of overclaiming elsewhere (amygdala, dopamine, Libet) but not here.
problems.fix: Add a one-line caveat: the popular 'dramatic personality transformation' story about Gage is now understood to be substantially embellished beyond the thin primary-source record (Macmillan, 2000); treat it as illustrative, not a rigorously documented case.

problems.issue: FFA card and recognize_face/reading_sentence pathways cite Gao et al. (2019, Psychophysiology) as establishing FFA/fusiform gyrus as 'the' N170 source. Verified via search: Gao et al. 2019 does support fusiform gyrus (including FFA) as a primary contributor, but competing intracranial work (e.g., studies implicating the inferior occipital gyrus/OFA) shows the field has not fully converged on a single source for the N170 — other face-selective regions (OFA, STS) also contribute in some studies.
problems.fix: Soften 'source-localizes the N170 face response to the fusiform gyrus/FFA' to 'identifies the fusiform gyrus/FFA as a primary (though likely not sole) contributor to the N170'.

problems.issue: The six named Izhikevich neuron-type presets (RS/IB/CH/FS/LTS/TC) are presented as if each (a,b,c,d) tuple alone deterministically produces its named firing pattern. This is true for RS/IB/CH/FS/LTS, but the TC (thalamocortical) preset's tonic-vs-rebound-burst behavior in Izhikevich's original model also depends on the neuron's baseline holding potential/current (e.g., needs a hyperpolarizing baseline to show rebound bursting), not just the four parameters.
problems.fix: Add a short note on the TC preset specifically: its bursting vs. tonic-firing behavior also depends on the background current/holding potential, not only (a,b,c,d).

problems.issue: The corpus_callosum card and split-brain framing omit the anterior commissure, which also carries some interhemispheric information (notably some olfactory and limbic/temporal-lobe information) and is clinically relevant to why some split-brain effects are partial rather than absolute.
problems.fix: Optional one-line addition noting the anterior commissure as a smaller secondary interhemispheric pathway not modeled here.

missing: A caveat parallel to the existing amygdala-fear-center warning, applied to Broca's/Wernicke's areas: the classic language localization model is considered obsolete by modern aphasiology and should be labeled a teaching simplification, not settled fact.
A caveat on the hypothalamus card noting the classic VMH-satiety/LH-hunger 'dual center' model is now considered outdated in light of arcuate-nucleus/leptin research.
A reconciliation note (or removal of one figure) for the two conflicting amygdala-latency citations used within the same fear_response pathway (20-30ms MEG vs. 74-88ms intracranial).
A corrected journal name for the Luo et al. 2007 citation (NeuroImage, not PNAS).

An explicit go/no-go decision on trimming v1 scope (fewer pathways/regions, or shipping one mode before all three) given the combined complexity of procedural 3D anatomy + animated pathway state machine + spiking-network simulation in a single zero-build-step file.
A caveat on the Phineas Gage case noting the popular narrative is more embellished than the thin primary-source record supports.

No verification was attempted (given time/effort budget) for: Padoa-Schioppa & Assad 2006 OFC value-coding specifics, O'Connell et al. 2012 CPP latency ranges, Staresina et al. 2015 slow-oscillation/spindle/ripple coupling specifics, Doyon 2003/2018 motor-learning stage timing, and Aston-Jones & Cohen 2005 adaptive gain theory specifics — these are well-known, frequently-cited findings in the field and were judged lower-risk, but were not independently re-verified via search in this pass.
